hints: Combine the two logarithms using the quotient law.
Multiply through by $y+4$, collect the terms containing $y$, and factor out $y$.
walkthrough:
Apply the quotient law for logarithms, $\ln A - \ln B = \ln\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)$:
$$x = \ln(2y - 3) - \ln(y + 4)$$
$$x = \ln\left(\dfrac{2y - 3}{y + 4}\right)$$

Exponentiate both sides with base $\mathrm{e}$ to eliminate the natural logarithm:
$$\mathrm{e}^x = \mathrm{e}^{\ln\left(\frac{2y - 3}{y + 4}\right)}$$
$$\mathrm{e}^x = \dfrac{2y - 3}{y + 4}$$

Multiply both sides by the denominator $(y + 4)$ to eliminate the fraction:
$$\mathrm{e}^x(y + 4) = 2y - 3$$
$$y\mathrm{e}^x + 4\mathrm{e}^x = 2y - 3$$

Rearrange the equation to collect all terms containing $y$ on one side and terms without $y$ on the other side:
$$4\mathrm{e}^x + 3 = 2y - y\mathrm{e}^x$$

Factor out $y$ from the right-hand side:
$$y(2 - \mathrm{e}^x) = 3 + 4\mathrm{e}^x$$

Divide both sides by $(2 - \mathrm{e}^x)$ to solve explicitly for $y$ in terms of $x$:
$$y = \dfrac{3 + 4\mathrm{e}^x}{2 - \mathrm{e}^x}$$
